title: The Howard's fourteen-piece band and playing Ben Hur for the silents
summary: The Howard job grew to a 14-piece pit band playing overtures and whole silent films; his ability to read got him the job.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How did you happen to get the job at the Howard? That would be a pretty good job.
It was, a doggone good job. Come to be finally we had a 14-piece band there, and was playing heavy because see Caroline was conducting, and we -- I played (finger snapping) Ben Hur in that theater.

I really did, because they had 'Ben Hur,' then they had to -- we had to get the music, and screened it, and get it together, and we did the chariot race and all that stuff, and this was like silent pictures. Back in the silent days.
You played for the whole picture?
And then you played for the show too?
Yeah, well yes. Because that's -- they had chorus girls, and all that business, you know.
But you were getting into the band. Now this must have been a job that everybody wanted. How did you manage to get in?

Well, being able to read helped tremendously, because for a job like that you couldn't sit down and kid yourself -- you'd be kidding yourself. You don't kid them. You know you have to be able to play as they call -- then they were calling it jazz, play the regular music, you know, classics, whatever, because we played a lot of overtures and stuff, because Caroline set it up. She knew what she wanted, and sometimes she could just -- recall for one thing, she suggest something else instead, the same, you know.
